### Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. In May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the US government stopped using the feature, with the aim of making civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

A separate step followed in September 2007, when the government announced that future GPS III satellites would be procured without Selective Availability. The 2000 action ended the feature’s use under the existing policy; the 2007 procurement choice carried that policy into a future generation.
